origin.description: This is an internal function to create a new github_remote, users should generally have no need for it.
origin.usage: github_remote(repo, ref = "HEAD", subdir = NULL, auth_token = github_pat(), sha = NULL, host = "api.github.com", ...)

arguments.name: repo
arguments.text: Repository address in the format username/repo[/subdir][@ref|#pull|@*release]. subdir and ref may also be arguments. When both are set, the values in repo take precedence.

arguments.name: ref
arguments.text: Commit, tag, or branch name, or a call to github_pull() or github_release(). Default "HEAD", the default branch.

arguments.name: subdir
arguments.text: Subdirectory within the repo that contains the R package.

arguments.name: auth_token
arguments.text: Personal access token for a private repo. The default is github_pat(), which the manual describes as the GITHUB_PAT environment variable.

arguments.name: sha
arguments.text: Commit SHA stored on the remote. Default NULL. The manual lists it in the usage and does not describe it.

arguments.name: host
arguments.text: GitHub API host. Default api.github.com. A GitHub Enterprise host looks like github.hostname.com/api/v3.
Other arguments passed on to utils::install.packages().

origin.details: The manual page has no example. parse_git_repo reads a GitHub URL when the text starts with https://github or git@github, and otherwise reads the shorthand. Fields whose nchar is 0 are dropped. An empty string is kept by %||% because it is not NULL. A remaining pull is stored as github_pull and a remaining release as github_release; those two refs are resolved through the GitHub API. A pull GET replaces username with head.user.login and ref with head.ref. A release GET stores the first tag_name. With the curl package installed, an HTTP error is parsed and appended: a missing pull adds HTTP error 404, Not Found, and the owner and repo spelling guidance. An empty release list stops with No releases found for repo. A string ref is stored as given, and NULL becomes HEAD. A parsed subdir wins over the subdir argument.
origin.value: An object of class github_remote and remote, with fields host, package, repo, subdir, username, ref, sha, and auth_token. A parsed field that was dropped is NULL.

translation.description: This is an internal function to create a new github_remote, users should generally have no need for it.
translation.usage: github_remote(repo, ref="HEAD", subdir=None, auth_token=<GITHUB_PAT or GITHUB_TOKEN>, sha=None, host="api.github.com", **extra)

arguments.name: repo
arguments.text: Repository address in the format username/repo[/subdir][@ref|#pull|@*release], or an https://github or git@github URL. A parsed subdir or ref wins over the argument.

arguments.name: ref
arguments.text: Commit, tag, or branch name, or github_pull() or github_release(). Default "HEAD". Used when the specification has no ref.

arguments.name: subdir
arguments.text: Subdirectory within the repo that contains the package. Used when the specification has no subdir.

arguments.name: auth_token
arguments.text: Personal access token. Omitted, the default reads GITHUB_PAT, then GITHUB_TOKEN, when the string is non-empty. If neither is set, the default is None. An explicit None stays None.

arguments.name: sha
arguments.text: Commit SHA stored on the remote. Default None. It is not looked up.

arguments.name: extra
arguments.text: Further arguments are accepted and ignored.

translation.details: Empty strings are dropped before %||% is applied, and an empty string that remains is kept. A parsed subdir wins over the subdir argument. A string ref is stored as that string, and None becomes HEAD. A github_pull GETs https://{host}/repos/{username}/{repo}/pulls/{number}, sends Authorization: token {pat} when auth_token is set, and replaces username with head.user.login and ref with head.ref. A github_release GETs the releases list and stores the first tag_name. An HTTP status at or above 300 stops with the installed github_error message. A 404 appends HTTP error 404, Not Found, and the owner and repo spelling guidance. A missing head, a JSON error message, or an empty release list stops with the same message as the installed function. The git credential store and the bundled CI token are not used.
translation.value: An object with class names github_remote and remote, and fields host, package, repo, subdir, username, ref, sha, and auth_token. A missing parsed field is None.
translation.example:
from remotes.github_remote import github_remote
x = github_remote("igraph=igraph/rigraph@v1.0.0", auth_token=None)
print('github_remote("igraph=igraph/rigraph@v1.0.0", auth_token = NULL) returns package ' + x.package + ', repo ' + x.repo + ', ref ' + x.ref + '.')
try:
    pull = github_remote("r-lib/remotes#7", auth_token=None)
    print('github_remote("r-lib/remotes#7", auth_token = NULL) returns username ' + pull.username + ', repo ' + pull.repo + ', ref ' + pull.ref + '.')
except RuntimeError as exc:
    print('github_remote("r-lib/remotes#7", auth_token = NULL) stops with:')
    print(exc)
